gaps.what: No Wikipedia article: the state page is a maintenance stub, so no infobox area or dated text for the row; built from five other pages.
Sao Tome, Fernando Po (Bioko) and the Zanzibar-Pemba-Mafia cells of the shape are not dated by any page opened; 1534 Inhambane and Zambezi-delta cells and 1564 Guinea (Cacheu) cells are confidence 1.

Agadir 1505-1541, Mogador 1506-1510 (portuguese-morocco), Kilwa 1505-1512 (kilwa-sultanate) and Malindi occupation 1500-1630 appear on the Evolution page but not in the Cliopatria shape; Malindi (no land or counterpart named) and Arguin's pre-1507 history are not in the ledger beyond the found event.

Holdings continue under Portugal after 1581 (Tangier to 1662, Mazagan to 1769, Elmina to 1637, Cape Verde, Mozambique, Angola) while Cliopatria draws them in its Spanish Empire row; no dossier of this batch covers 1582-1640 for the cells.

The 1842 Oran-Tlemcen-Mascara block and the 1846 jump to 211,876 km2 (including the southern limit near 33.6 N) are not dated or delimited by the five pages; gap-filler should open Capture of the Smala, Conquest of Kabylia and Laghouat.
Oran 1830-1832 and Bone 1830-1833: the pages disagree on when the French held them; the Cliopatria cells stand unverified.
Dedicated pages Invasion of Algiers in 1830, Siege of Constantine (1837), Capture of the Smala were not opened; dates come from the French Algeria and conquest pages.

problems: portuguese-africa overlaps portuguese-morocco, portuguese-mozambique, portuguese-angola and portuguese-empire for 1507-1581: the integrator must draw each cell once; this dossier keeps the whole Cliopatria shape (see its notes for the suggested split).

Cliopatria closes Portuguese Africa in 1581 and draws all 99 cells in its Spanish Empire row from 1582 (the Iberian Union row holds none) although the pages show them still Portuguese; the dossier's successor is spanish-empire with a note, and 1582-1640 needs an owner.
The Wikipedia article 'Portuguese Africa' is a stub; identity.wikipedia keeps Cliopatria's title.
french-algeria ends in 1847 (Cliopatria) while the page runs the colony to 1848 and part of France to 1962; french-africa takes Algeria from 1848.
french-algeria uses counterpart beylik-of-constantine (no dossier; 2 validator warnings) and its Emirate contest pair ends 23 December 1847 while emirate-of-abdelkader ends its contests in 1846.

WebFetch returned model summaries of pages, not raw text: quotation marks appear only where the tool showed words in quotes. The French Algeria and conquest pages differ on the annexation date (22 July vs 22 June 1834).
Page budget: portuguese-africa used six fetches including the empty state article (five content pages); french-algeria used five.
